ready.title: Multi-Qubit States and Gates
ready.hook: The state of n qubits has 2^n amplitudes, and a two-qubit gate is what lets them stop being independent.

ready.title: Manifolds and Tensors
ready.hook: A tensor is an object whose components change in a prescribed way with the coordinates, so that equations built from tensors hold in every coordinate system.

ready.title: Parameterized Circuits
ready.hook: A parameterized circuit is a function from angles to an expectation value, which turns quantum computation into an optimization problem for a classical computer.

ready.title: Phase Transitions
ready.hook: A phase transition is a point where a thermodynamic potential stops being smooth, and the critical point is where the two phases become one.
leads_to: Interacting Gases and the van der Waals Equation

ready.title: Line and Surface Integrals
ready.hook: Work is a line integral and flux is a surface integral; both measure a field against a geometry.
leads_to: Divergence, Curl and the Integral Theorems

ready.title: The Displacement Current
ready.hook: Ampère's law as stated fails for a charging capacitor; adding a term for the changing electric field repairs it and is the step that makes waves possible.

ready.title: The Fourier Transform
ready.hook: The transform trades a function of position for a function of frequency, and a narrow signal is broad in the other variable.

ready.title: Categories and Morphisms
ready.hook: A category forgets what the objects are made of and keeps only the arrows between them and how they compose.
figures: commuting triangle and the category of a poset as a diagram
verify: identities and composition are unique
an isomorphism has a unique inverse

ready.title: Multi-Electron Atoms
ready.hook: Electrons are indistinguishable fermions, and filling shells under the Pauli principle explains the periodic table.

ready.title: Markov Chain Monte Carlo
ready.hook: A random walk built to satisfy detailed balance visits states with their Boltzmann weights, so one can simulate a magnet on a laptop.
leads_to: Random Walks and the Metropolis Algorithm

ready.title: Homomorphisms and Quotients
ready.hook: A homomorphism is a map that respects the operation, and its kernel is exactly what a quotient group divides out.
figures: cosets of a subgroup of Z_12 coloured on a clock face
verify: the kernel of a homomorphism is a normal subgroup
G/ker f is isomorphic to the image of f

ready.title: Transformations and Quaternions
ready.hook: Rotation, translation and scaling become a single matrix product in homogeneous coordinates, and quaternions give rotations that compose and interpolate cleanly.

ready.title: Singular Value Decomposition
ready.hook: Every matrix is a rotation, a stretch along perpendicular axes and another rotation; the stretches say how much of the matrix is worth keeping.
leads_to: Composite Systems and the Schmidt Decomposition

ready.title: Crystal Structure
ready.hook: A crystal is a lattice with a motif, and diffraction measures its reciprocal lattice.

ready.title: Inductance and Magnetic Energy
ready.hook: A coil resists changes in its own current because the field it makes links its own turns; that resistance, inductance, is the magnetic counterpart of capacitance.
leads_to: Energy and Momentum in the Field

ready.title: Kernel Methods
ready.hook: A kernel computes the inner product of two examples in a huge feature space without building that space, so linear methods become nonlinear for free.

ready.title: Partial Differential Equations
ready.hook: Three equations, one for diffusion, one for waves and one for equilibrium, cover most of mathematical physics, and separating variables reduces each to ordinary ones.

ready.title: Neutral-Atom Qubits and Pulses
ready.hook: A laser pulse of the right area and phase is a rotation of the Bloch sphere, so the pulse sequence is the circuit.

ready.title: Numerical Linear Algebra
ready.hook: The cost and the accuracy of a linear solve are set by the structure and conditioning of the matrix.

ready.title: Potentials and Gauge Freedom
ready.hook: Two of Maxwell's equations are solved at once by writing the fields as derivatives of potentials, and the potentials are not unique: that freedom is the first example of a gauge symmetry.

ready.title: Nearest Neighbours and the Curse of Dimensionality
ready.hook: The simplest predictor averages the closest examples, and it works until the space is so large that nothing is close.

ready.title: Non-Inertial Frames and Rigid Bodies
ready.hook: Accelerating observers see extra forces, and a spinning body has an inertia that depends on direction.

ready.title: Dielectrics
ready.hook: An insulator in a field has its charges nudged into dipoles, which weakens the field inside; the displacement field bookkeeps only the charges you control.

ready.title: Matrix Groups and Lie Algebras
ready.hook: Continuous symmetries are groups of matrices, and differentiating at the identity gives a vector space that remembers the group.
figures: rotation group SO(2) as a circle and the exponential map
verify: so(3) is spanned by three antisymmetric generators with [Lx, Ly] = Lz
exp of an antisymmetric matrix is a rotation

ready.title: Natural Gradient
ready.hook: Plain gradient descent depends on how the parameters are written, and the natural gradient removes that by measuring steps with the Fisher information.

ready.title: Laurent Series and Residues
ready.hook: A contour integral is fixed by the singularities it encloses, which turns hard real integrals into bookkeeping.

ready.title: Testing and Performance
ready.hook: A renderer has no right answer to compare against, so correctness comes from tests against cases with known results and from measuring where the time goes.

ready.title: Heat Engines and Refrigerators
ready.hook: No engine between two temperatures beats the Carnot engine, and the bound depends only on the two temperatures.

blocked.title: The Metric and Causal Structure
blocked.hook: The metric turns coordinates into measured intervals, and its signature divides spacetime into what can and cannot influence a point.

blocked.title: Gradients and the Parameter-Shift Rule
blocked.hook: On hardware the gradient of a rotation parameter is an exact difference of two circuit runs at shifted angles, with no finite-difference error.

blocked.title: Covariant Derivative and Geodesics
blocked.hook: Free fall is motion along the straightest possible path in curved spacetime, and the Christoffel symbols are what Newton called the gravitational field.

blocked.title: The Variational Quantum Eigensolver
blocked.hook: The energy of any trial state bounds the ground energy from above, so minimising it over circuit parameters approaches the ground state from above.

blocked.title: Curvature
blocked.hook: Curvature is what remains when you try to move a vector around a loop and it fails to return, and geodesic deviation turns it into tidal forces.

blocked.title: Radiometry and the Rendering Equation
blocked.hook: The light leaving a point is what it emits plus what it reflects of the light arriving from everywhere else, which is an integral equation whose solution is the image.

blocked.title: Bell States and Entanglement
blocked.hook: A Bell state has a pure joint state and a maximally mixed part, and the same correlations appear in every basis, which no product state can do.
leads_to: Composite Systems and the Schmidt Decomposition

blocked.title: The Einstein Equations
blocked.hook: Spacetime tells matter how to move and matter tells spacetime how to curve: the Einstein tensor is set equal to the stress-energy tensor.

blocked.title: Functors
blocked.hook: A functor maps one category into another and keeps composition, which is why it carries structure across.
figures: a functor sending a commuting square to a commuting square
verify: a functor sends isomorphisms to isomorphisms
the composite of functors is a functor

blocked.title: The Transverse-Field Ising Model
blocked.hook: The model has an exact free-fermion solution, which is why it serves as the ground truth against which circuits are measured.

blocked.title: Materials, BRDFs and Shading
blocked.hook: A material is a function that says how light arriving from one direction leaves towards another, and a plausible one must conserve energy.

blocked.title: Shapes and Intersections
blocked.hook: Everything a renderer does asks one question, where does this ray first hit the scene, and the answer depends on how the objects are described.

blocked.title: Natural Transformations
blocked.hook: A natural transformation is a family of arrows that commutes with everything, and Yoneda says an object is its arrows.
figures: naturality square for double dual of a vector space
verify: the evaluation map V to V** is natural
Nat(Hom(A,-), F) is isomorphic to F(A)

blocked.title: Electromagnetic Waves
blocked.hook: In empty space the four equations combine into a wave equation whose speed is fixed by two constants measured on a bench, and that speed is the speed of light.
leads_to: Energy and Momentum in the Field

blocked.title: The Schwarzschild Solution
blocked.hook: Outside any spherical mass the geometry is fixed, and its orbits differ from Kepler's in ways that can be measured.

blocked.title: Group Actions
blocked.hook: A group action turns abstract symmetries into permutations of something you can see, and counting orbits becomes a formula.
figures: orbits of the dihedral group on the vertices and edges of a square
verify: |G| = |orbit| times |stabiliser|
Burnside: the number of orbits is the average number of fixed points

blocked.title: Ray Tracing
blocked.hook: Following rays backwards from the eye finds what is visible, and spawning more rays at each hit adds shadows, mirrors and glass.

blocked.title: Multi-Controlled Gates and Circuit Depth
blocked.hook: A gate with n controls cannot be built from a few elementary gates, and the measured depth is what makes the cost of a decomposition concrete.

blocked.title: The Free Electron Model
blocked.hook: Metals behave as a gas of electrons that fill states up to the Fermi energy, and only electrons near that energy matter.

blocked.title: Universal Properties and Limits
blocked.hook: A product, a quotient or a free object is defined not by its elements but by the unique map it admits.
figures: product diagram with its unique mediating arrow
verify: products in sets are cartesian products
a universal object is unique up to unique isomorphism

blocked.title: Colour and Colour Spaces
blocked.hook: Colour is how a spectrum is seen by three kinds of receptor, so a renderer can work in three numbers when it treats them with care.

blocked.title: Monte Carlo Path Tracing
blocked.hook: The rendering equation is an integral over paths of light, and a random walk through the scene estimates it without bias at the cost of noise.

blocked.title: Oracles and Phase Kickback
blocked.hook: An oracle is a black box, and phase kickback is the trick that moves its answer from a register into a relative phase that interference can use.

blocked.title: Trainability and Barren Plateaus
blocked.hook: For generic deep circuits the gradient is exponentially small in the number of qubits, so structure in the ansatz is a requirement and not a refinement.

blocked.title: The Rydberg Blockade
blocked.hook: Two atoms close together cannot both be excited, which is a conditional operation that comes directly from the physics instead of from a gate decomposition.

blocked.title: Composite Systems and the Schmidt Decomposition
blocked.hook: Any pure state of two systems can be written with a single sum over paired basis vectors, and the number of terms and their weights decide how entangled it is.

blocked.title: Band Theory
blocked.hook: A periodic potential opens gaps in the energy spectrum, and whether the top band is full decides whether the solid conducts.

blocked.title: Divergence, Curl and the Integral Theorems
blocked.hook: Divergence measures how much a field spreads out and curl how much it circulates; the theorems say that totals over a region are fixed by what happens on its boundary.

blocked.title: Adjunctions
blocked.hook: Adjoint functors are the best possible approximate inverses, and they turn up wherever something is free or a quotient.
figures: free-forgetful adjunction between sets and vector spaces
verify: hom(F A, B) is naturally isomorphic to hom(A, G B)
right adjoints preserve limits

blocked.title: Monoidal Categories and Diagrams
blocked.hook: A monoidal category adds a way to put objects side by side, and string diagrams then compute with pictures.
figures: string diagram of a quantum circuit
verify: the tensor product of vector spaces is associative up to natural isomorphism

blocked.title: Finite Differences for PDEs
blocked.hook: Replacing derivatives by differences turns a field equation into a recurrence, and its stability decides whether it is usable.

blocked.title: Energy and Momentum in the Field
blocked.hook: The energy in the field flows, and the Poynting vector says where; a wave carries energy and momentum with it.

blocked.title: Electromagnetism and Relativity
blocked.hook: A magnetic field in one frame is partly an electric field in another, so the two are components of one object whose equations are the same in every inertial frame.

blocked.title: Classical Tests
blocked.hook: Four measurable effects, each a few lines from the Schwarzschild geodesics, are what first made the theory credible.

blocked.title: Black Holes
blocked.hook: A black hole is a region from which nothing returns, and the horizon is a feature of the geometry rather than a place where anything special happens locally.

blocked.title: Gravitational Waves
blocked.hook: Small ripples of the metric obey a wave equation, travel at the speed of light and carry energy away from accelerating masses.

blocked.title: Cosmology
blocked.hook: If the universe is the same everywhere on large scales, the field equations reduce to two equations for a single scale factor.

blocked.title: Symmetric and Dihedral Groups
blocked.hook: Every finite group sits inside a symmetric group, and the dihedral groups are the symmetries of a regular polygon.
figures: the six symmetries of a triangle
verify: the symmetric group S_n has n! elements
the dihedral group D_n has 2n elements

blocked.title: Structure of Finite Groups
blocked.hook: A finite group is assembled from simple pieces, and Sylow theory says which subgroups must exist.
verify: the number of Sylow p-subgroups is 1 mod p and divides the index

blocked.title: Representations and Characters
blocked.hook: A representation lets a group act on a vector space, and its character is the number that tells irreducible pieces apart.
figures: character table of the symmetric group S_3 as a coloured grid
verify: sum of squared dimensions of irreducibles equals the group order
characters of distinct irreducibles are orthogonal

blocked.title: Support Vector Machines
blocked.hook: Among all separating hyperplanes the one farthest from the data generalizes best, and only the points on the margin decide it.

blocked.title: Distributions and Green's Functions
blocked.hook: The response to a point source solves the problem for every source, which is the idea behind propagators and the potential of a point charge.

blocked.title: Special Functions
blocked.hook: The angular and radial parts of the Laplacian in spherical and cylindrical coordinates give polynomials and functions that reappear in electrostatics and in the hydrogen atom.

blocked.title: Encoding Images
blocked.hook: A display shows a few hundred levels while a scene spans many orders of magnitude, so the numbers have to be mapped and encoded before they are shown.

blocked.title: Filtering and Antialiasing
blocked.hook: A pixel is an average over an area, and sampling it badly gives jagged edges that no later processing can repair.

blocked.title: GHZ and W States
blocked.hook: With three qubits there are two kinds of genuine entanglement that no local operations can convert into each other, and GHZ and W are their representatives.

blocked.title: Grover Search
blocked.hook: Grover rotates the state by a fixed angle toward the marked item at each step, so sqrt(N) steps suffice and more steps overshoot.

blocked.title: The Quantum Fourier Transform
blocked.hook: The QFT applies the discrete Fourier transform to the amplitudes with about n squared gates instead of N log N, but the output cannot be read out in full.

blocked.title: QUBO, QAOA and Adiabatic Algorithms
blocked.hook: A binary optimization problem is the ground-state search of an Ising Hamiltonian, which an atom register realises with its own interaction.

blocked.title: Finite-Size Scaling and Criticality
blocked.hook: On a finite chain the transition is rounded, and the way it sharpens with size gives the critical field and the exponents.

blocked.title: Entanglement Entropy and Central Charge
blocked.hook: Away from criticality the entropy saturates, at criticality it grows as a logarithm whose coefficient is the central charge, and an open boundary biases the fit.

blocked.title: Ansatz Comparison: HEA versus HVA
blocked.hook: An ansatz shaped like the Hamiltonian reaches a lower energy error and stays trainable as the chain grows, where a generic one does not.

blocked.title: Classical Shadows
blocked.hook: Random single-qubit measurements are enough to estimate many observables later, with a variance that depends on the observable and not on the number of qubits.

blocked.title: Bell and CHSH Inequalities
blocked.hook: No theory in which measurement results are fixed in advance and independent of distant choices can reproduce the correlations of an entangled pair.

blocked.title: No-Cloning and Teleportation
blocked.hook: An unknown quantum state cannot be copied, but it can be moved, using a shared Bell pair and two classical bits.

blocked.title: Quantum Channels and Kraus Operators
blocked.hook: Noise is what happens when a system interacts with an environment it is not watching, and the result is a map on density matrices of a fixed form.

blocked.title: Von Neumann Entropy
blocked.hook: Entropy of a quantum state is the Shannon entropy of its eigenvalues, and for a pure state of two systems it measures their entanglement.

waiting.title: Composite Systems and the Schmidt Decomposition

blocked.title: Atomic Spectra and Selection Rules
blocked.hook: Spin-orbit coupling splits the hydrogen lines, and symmetry decides which transitions are allowed.

blocked.title: Molecules and Bonding
blocked.hook: A bond is the lowering of energy when electrons are shared, and the motion of the nuclei gives a ladder of rotational and vibrational levels.

blocked.title: Semiconductors
blocked.hook: Doping puts carriers in a band that would otherwise be empty, and the p-n junction is where that becomes a diode.
